Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

specify verb

state exactly

also be specific, state expressly, specified

classical

Cic. Off. 3.65: nisi nōminātim dictum esset

nōminātim dīcere

phrase

specify, state expressly

Nōminātim is “by name, one by one, expressly”, and goes with any verb of saying or naming: nōminātim excipere, to except by name (Cic. Att. 11.7.2).

Other words

  • dēfīniō, dēfīnīre, dēfīnīvī, dēfīnītum — fix, set exactly (a time, a term, a limit)

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. B.C. 3.82.4; Quint. 12.6.1 (Lewis & Short)

    To set bounds to, and so to fix; for its sense “define”, see define.

  • praescrībō, praescrībere, praescrīpsī, praescrīptum — lay down, prescribe (what is to be done)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.26.2: sīc enim praescrīpsimus (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • id statuērunt, sī venditor scīret, nisi nōminātim dictum esset, praestārī oportēre.

    they ruled that, if the seller knew of the defect, he must make it good, unless it had been expressly stated.Cic. Off. 3.65

  • ibi ego dīcam quidquid inerit nōminātim

    I’ll tell you everything that’s in it, item by itemPlaut. Rud. 1134

See also define.
